Port bpo-39057 to Requests

This PR ports a [fix](https://bugs.python.org/issue39057) from CPython to constrain no_proxy behavior to domain boundaries. This was originally undefined behavior when Requests implemented `no_proxy` support but has since had bug fixes released in both CPython and Curl. turns.reply:
I've ported the bpo-39057 fix: a `no_proxy` entry now only matches whole domain names. Before, `example.com` in `no_proxy` also bypassed the proxy for `notexample.com`; now it doesn't.

The change is in `should_bypass_proxies` in `src/requests/utils.py`. The old code just checked whether the hostname ended with the entry's text. Now, for each entry:
- Leading dots are removed, so `.example.com` and `example.com` mean the same thing.
- The entry matches if it equals the hostname, or if the hostname ends with `.` plus the entry. The same check runs against `host:port`.
- Matching now ignores upper/lower case. That wasn't in the original code; I added it to line up with CPython's behaviour.
- Entries that are empty after stripping (such as a lone `.`) are skipped.

IP and CIDR entries work as before. Requests still falls back to Python's own `proxy_bypass` afterwards, as it did before.

**Testing:** the proxy and bypass tests in `tests/test_utils.py` pass (73 passed, 12 skipped). A quick manual check gave the expected results:
- `notexample.com` against `example.com`: not bypassed
- `a.example.com` against `example.com`: bypassed
- `example.com:80` against `.example.com`: bypassed
- `a.example.com:8080` against `example.com:8080`: bypassed

I didn't add a new test for the `notexample.com` case, so the existing suite doesn't cover the fix yet.
